description:
TURN BACK INTO THE MAN. THREE TABLE BYTES, ONE PURPOSE: a player who has just been barged off balance may contest instead of spectating. This is the 'physical battles' pack. Test it THIRD, alone.

THE PROBLEM. While the current action is a Stagger, the eligibility filter (vtable slot 2, canStart) refuses Tackle, Feint and Reaction OUTRIGHT - not late, not gated, refused at every frame. Emulated at frame 120, long after every cancel key has passed, all three are still dropped. So there is no such thing as losing a shoulder-to-shoulder and immediately fighting back: the engine ends the contest the moment contact is made and hands it to whoever was not knocked. Contact is currently a full stop, and this pack makes it a comma.

WHAT CHANGES. Each action's vf2 is a switch on the CURRENT action's kind, implemented as a byte table indexed by (currentKind - 2). Stagger is 0x10, so the entry is at table + 0x0e. Three entries move off the 'refuse' handler and onto the existing 'ask the current action whether it may be interrupted' handler:
    Tackle::vf2   table 0x143f7cae0, entry 0x143f7caee : 3 -> 1
    Feint::vf2    table 0x143fabb44, entry 0x143fabb52 : 1 -> 0
    Reaction::vf2 table 0x143f6d8e0, entry 0x143f6d8ee : 1 -> 0
No handler is created and no code is written - each byte just selects a case that the same table already uses for other current kinds.

MEASURED EFFECT (a-EMULATED, this pass, end to end through the REAL requester 0x143eb4f40 -> vf2 -> Stagger::vf14 -> starter). First frame the request starts, current action = Stagger, test motion with cancel keys at 16/32/48:
    request           stock     THIS PACK
    Tackle            never      16
    Feint             never      16
    Reaction          never      16
    (Dribble          48         48   - untouched, that is contact-dribble-cancel-early.json)
    (Move             never      never - untouched, that is contact-move-out-of-stagger.json)

HOW IT KEEPS THE WEIGHT, AND A TRAP I CHECKED FOR YOU. Each of these tables has more than one 'yes' value, and they are NOT equivalent. I swept every candidate value 0-4 through the real code. For Tackle, value 2 also lets the request through - but it is the ALLOW-OUTRIGHT handler: it starts at frame 0, the cancel gate is never consulted, and the stagger is erased entirely. Value 1 is the gated handler and opens at frame 16. This pack uses the GATED values in all three cases, so the stumble still has to reach its first cancel keyframe before you can swing. Anyone tempted to 'just set it to 2' would silently delete the weight.
    Tackle   0x143f7caee : 0=gated@16  1=gated@16  2=OUTRIGHT@0  3=refuse(stock)  -> using 1
    Feint    0x143fabb52 : 0=gated@16  1=refuse(stock)                            -> using 0
    Reaction 0x143f6d8ee : 0=gated@16  1=refuse(stock)                            -> using 0

EVIDENCE.
  a-EMULATED - every value above, run on the game's own bytes under Unicorn through the real request chain. Harness tools/emu_contact_request.py, output build/emu_contact_request_proof.txt sections 5 and 7.
  b-DISASSEMBLY - the three switch tables and their index arithmetic: Tackle::vf2 0x143f7ca30 'lea eax,[rdx-2] / cmp eax,0x52 / ja refuse / movzx eax,byte[0x143f7cae0+rax]'; Feint::vf2 0x143fabac0 table 0x143fabb44 (read off 'movzx eax, byte ptr [r8+rax+0x3fabb44]'); Reaction::vf2 0x143f6d870 table 0x143f6d8e0.
  NOTE - an earlier pass reported Feint::vf2 as 0x143fabb10. That is wrong; the vtable slot-2 entry is 0x143fabac0. The table address it quoted was right.

WHO IT AFFECTS: EVERYONE. These tables are per-class, not per-player, and contain no cursor or team test. CPU defenders will also fight back out of stumbles, which is the point.

WHAT YOU SHOULD SEE IN ONE MATCH. A midfielder who gets shoulder-charged should be able to spin and put a foot in rather than jogging off the contact. Watch for scrappy two-and-three-touch exchanges in central midfield that stock just do not happen.

EXPECTED EFFECT ON FOULS AND CARDS: MORE OF BOTH, and this is the one pack here that really does move the referee. It manufactures challenges that could not previously exist. The foul model is untouched and will judge them normally - scorer 0x143d88fe0, threshold 40 outside the box and 60 inside, cards at 80 and 110 - but the repeat-offender escalation at 0x143d87511 adds count/3 to the score BEFORE the level is computed, so a player who keeps fighting back climbs toward a card faster. Do NOT test this pack in the same session as phys-reckless-contact or phys-whistle-threshold.

WHAT WOULD MEAN IT IS TOO FAR. Two things, and watch for both. (1) Cards: if you are seeing yellows you would not have conceded, drop the Tackle byte and keep Feint and Reaction. (2) The PICTURE, not the feel: these bytes change which animations may blend into which, and the game's animators never authored 'tackle out of a stumble pose'. If a challenge visibly sprouts out of a stagger with a snap or a foot-slide, that is this pack and it is the failure mode the timing levers cannot produce.

COLLISIONS. All three sites verified byte-identical between the INSTALLED image and eFootball.exe.PRISTINE this pass (0x143f7caee=03, 0x143fabb52=01, 0x143f6d8ee=01). No overlap with any of the 26 applied specs. Orthogonal to the other contact packs - verified in the emulated matrix, where this pack leaves the Dribble, Move and floor rows exactly at stock.

IF YOU WANT LESS: apply only the Feint and Reaction bytes. They add shielding and reaching without adding a single challenge for the referee to judge, so they carry none of the card risk.

REVERT: python tools/exe_patch.py remove tools/data/patches/contact-fight-back-from-stagger.json

patches.name: Tackle::vf2 - a staggering player may ask to tackle (gated handler, not allow-outright)
patches.note: Entry (Stagger 0x10 - 2 = 0x0e) of the switch byte-table at 0x143f7cae0 inside match::anime::action::Tackle::vf2 (0x143f7ca30). Case 3 is the bare refuse tail at 0x143f7cac5; case 1 is the existing handler at 0x143f7ca9f that fetches the running action and calls its vf14 with requested kind 0x0d. Case 2 would also admit the request but is the ALLOW-OUTRIGHT path (emulated: starts at frame 0, no gate) and is deliberately NOT used. The sibling byte at 0x143f7caef (FallDown) is deliberately left alone - a man on the floor lunging into a tackle is the ugly case.

patches.name: Feint::vf2 - a staggering player may ask to shield / body-feint
patches.note: Entry (Stagger) of the switch byte-table at 0x143fabb44 inside match::anime::action::Feint::vf2 (0x143fabac0, vtable slot 2 - note an earlier pass mis-reported this function as 0x143fabb10). Case 1 is refuse; case 0 asks the running action's vf14. Emulated: refused at every frame -> opens at the first cancel key. Lowest-risk byte in this pack: a feint is a short blend and adds no challenge for the referee.

patches.name: Reaction::vf2 - a staggering player may ask to react to the ball
patches.note: Entry (Stagger) of the switch byte-table at 0x143f6d8e0 inside match::anime::action::Reaction::vf2 (0x143f6d870). Case 1 is refuse; case 0 asks the running action's vf14 with requested kind 0x14. Emulated: refused at every frame -> opens at the first cancel key.
